— Analytics & measurement

Know what your marketing is doing.

Marketing decisions need trustworthy signals. I help businesses define useful conversions, review their tracking, and build reporting that explains what happened and what remains uncertain.

Discuss analytics & measurement

A connected approach to analytics & measurement

A measurement plan starts with business questions. A service business may need to distinguish a button click from a delivered inquiry and a qualified opportunity. A store may need reliable transaction identifiers and consistent product data. Collecting more events does not automatically answer those questions. The useful work is defining each action, deciding where it can be observed, and verifying that reports describe that action accurately.

When this work can help

  • Dashboards disagree and no one knows which numbers to trust.
  • Clicks are counted as leads even when no message is delivered.
  • Tags have accumulated without clear ownership, consent rules, or documentation.

How I approach the work

I review the website journey, current tags, consent behavior, analytics property, and business reporting needs. We agree a concise event dictionary and identify gaps, duplicates, or misleading definitions. Changes are tested through the actual user journey, with debugging tools and destination reports used together. Access and publishing responsibilities are established before a container is changed.

Core activities & deliverables

Measurement plan

Define events, permitted parameters, conversion criteria, and reporting questions. Keep personal information and message contents out of analytics payloads.

Implementation and review

Configure or review GA4 and Google Tag Manager, validate triggers and consent states, and check duplication. Record genuine outcomes separately from early indicators such as form starts.

Reporting and handover

Create views that connect channels, landing pages, and meaningful actions. Explain attribution limits, document the setup, and define how future site changes will be checked.

Who this is for

This service suits businesses starting measurement, questioning an existing setup, or preparing to spend more on advertising. It can also support a redesign or migration where tracking needs to survive changes to pages and forms. Useful access may include the site, tag manager, analytics, advertising accounts, and the systems used to assess lead quality, depending on the agreed scope.

What to consider before starting

Consent choices, browser protections, ad blockers, cross-device use, and platform modelling limit observation. Analytics does not provide a perfect record of every customer journey. Legal requirements and data retention choices need appropriate business and legal review. A tracking implementation should avoid collecting sensitive data and cannot be treated as automatic proof of compliance.

How we assess progress

Readiness means that test actions produce the expected event once, withheld consent prevents prohibited tags, and failed submissions do not become successful conversions. Ongoing quality checks compare reporting trends with actual business records where possible. Sudden changes should trigger diagnosis of the collection system before they are interpreted as changes in demand.

Questions about analytics & measurement

Is Google Tag Manager the same as GA4?+

No. GTM deploys and manages tags; GA4 receives and reports analytics data. A GTM container ID and a GA4 measurement ID are different identifiers.

Can you recover missing historical data?+

Data that was never collected generally cannot be recreated. A review can explain gaps and establish a more reliable baseline going forward.
